Subject: Post-call: model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail - next steps

Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks again for your time earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

1) Use case summary
- Primary: product search relevance & reranking for web + mobile (top-k).
- Secondary: conversational shopping assistant for complex queries.
- Weighted success metrics: CTR lift on search results, top-3 relevance, and user satisfaction surveys for assistant.

2) Performance targets you called out
- Target p95 latency for in-session rerank: <= 250 ms (we discussed 200–300ms window).
- Throughput expectation: sustained ~400 QPS for peak search traffic (bursty patterns).
- Data requirements: PII redaction + SOC2 evidence (we'll loop security).

3) Recommended immediate evals
- Run Redwood eval harness on your canonical prompt set (attached acme_prompt_set_v1.csv).
- Compare two model candidates: rw-medium-quantized (lower cost, good latency) and rw-large-v1 (higher quality on long-tail).
- We'll run a 1k-query sanity run + 10k synthetic workload to surface regressions.

4) Deliverables from Redwood (what I can share right away)
- Redwood-verified performance profile (summary attached + link below).
- Prompt set we used as a starting point (attached).
- Mutual action plan with proposed dates (see below).

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_acme_retail_20260228.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (csv, 48KB)
Links: https://redwood-internal-benchmarks.company/benchmarks/ACME-2026-02

Proposed next steps (please pick):
- Option A: Tech check + sandbox eval (we provision a temporary sandbox and run the 1k-query run) — target week of Mar 2nd.
- Option B: Kick off security questionnaire and schedule a joint architecture review (if you need Private/VPC).

If you confirm Option A, I’ll ask Dylan to provision the eval environment and Logan to coordinate the benchmark config.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to align.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A couple quick questions before we lock dates:

- Can you share p50/p95/p99 latencies and tokens-per-second (TPS) for the two recommended models under a 512-token context? We want exact percentile numbers you measured (helps our SREs).
- How sensitive are these profiles to prompt engineering? We have some long product-description prompts that historically cause regressions.
- On security: we’ll need SOC 2 evidence and a pointer to where you host logs for audit. We’ll start the questionnaire but want to confirm whether a hosted (Redwood API) or Private deployment is recommended for our data model.

If you can send the perf snapshots and an annotated prompt-set example, we’ll pick Option A or B by EOD.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail - next steps

Hi Sam — great questions. See the quick Redwood-verified perf snapshots below (these are summary numbers from our benchmark run attached). I also note caveats and next actions after the table.

Redwood-verified performance profiles (stable measurements):

Model: rw-medium-quantized (recommended for cost-sensitive rerank)
- Measured config: region us-west-2, Dedicated cluster (8x A100 80GB), steady-state concurrency 16, seq len: 512 in / 64 out
- Tokens/sec (aggregate): 3,400 TPS
- Request latency (median / p95 / p99): 95 ms / 260 ms / 430 ms
- Cost note: ~0.6x unit cost vs rw-large-v1 for same workload

Model: rw-large-v1 (recommended for long-tail quality + assistant use cases)
- Measured config: same as above
- Tokens/sec (aggregate): 2,100 TPS
- Request latency (median / p95 / p99): 140 ms / 320 ms / 520 ms
- Quality note: shows +6–9% improvement on long-tail relevance F1 vs rw-medium on our retail prompt suite

Caveats & notes:
- These numbers are from our standard benchmarking harness (steady-state synthetic load + replay of your sample prompts). Real production numbers will vary with prompt length, batch sizes, and caching.
- Prompt engineering matter: for a portion of your long product-description prompts we saw quality variance — we recommend running the attached acme_prompt_set_v1.csv through our eval harness (we can run it on your behalf) and flag any regen candidates.
- Security: SOC 2 report + evidence links are available — I’ll share the secure doc link in parallel with Dylan. Hosted API is fine for most customers; for regulated data we recommend Private (VPC) — we can scope.

Next actions I suggest:
- Redwood runs the 1k-query sandbox eval on your canonical prompt set (we’ll return detailed per-query outputs + quality diffs).
- If results look good, run the 10k synthetic peak test to validate p95 under burst.
- Schedule a 30-min SRE sync (you, Raj, Logan, Dylan) to align on production sizing and logging.

I’ve attached the benchmark PDF for the full trace and the prompt set CSV for your review.

If that sounds good, Sam, please reply with preferred dates and whether you want us to provision a temporary sandbox under your account or run it inside a Redwood test tenant.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood_benchmark_acme_retail_20260228.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
